newsitem.title: USA: SOCCER-LATE GOAL GIVES ECUADOR 1-0 WIN OVER U.S. IN FRIENDLY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LATE GOAL GIVES ECUADOR 1-0 WIN OVER U.S. IN FRIENDLY.

text.p: A late goal by midfielder Wellington Sanchez gave Ecuador a 1-0 victory in an international soccer friendly on Thursday.
Ecuador broke through in the 83rd minute on a controversial goal when defender Jimmy Blandon hit a long lobbing ball from just outside his own penalty area to the fast-moving Sanchez.

When Sanchez collected the ball 40 metres from goal he appeared to be well ahead of the trapping U.S. defence, which could not stop him dribbling in on goal and slotting a shot past goalkeeper Brad Friedel into the lower right corner.
U.S. coach Steve Sampson said he thought Sanchez had been five to 10 metres offsides.

Prior to that goal, Ecuador's best chance came in the first half when Ariel Graziani, one of seven Ecuadoran players who played in the team's last World Cup qualifier, blasted the ball from seven metres right at Friedel.

The Americans' best scoring chance came in the 61st minute when midfielder Brian Maisonneuve, playing in just his second international match, collected a deflected shot by Preki Radosavijevic and fired a five-metre shot just wide of the goal.

The United States started eight players who had not played an international match in at least six months including two-time World Cup veteran Tab Ramos, who sparked the team's creative midfield play in an impressive return to the U.S. national team.
The 30-year-old midfielder injured his knee more than eight months ago, while playing for the United States in World Cup qualifying.
The Americans were playing a final tuneup for their next World Cup qualifying match on September 7 against Costa Rica in Portland, Oregon.

The Americans are in third place in CONCACAF with six points and a 1-1-3 record. Three of the remaining six CONCACAF (North, Central America and Caribbean) teams will advance to the 1998 World Cup final field of 32 in France.
